chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Hisham who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Would it suffice me if I were to say in place of the Glorification during the Rukū and the Sajdah,
There is no god except for Allah and Allah is the Greatest

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god except Allah)

ai.seo_question: What can be recited in place of the specific tasbih during ruku and sujud in prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of substituting the recommended glorifications in ruku' and sujud with the concise declaration of monotheism and divine greatness, 'La ilaha illa Allah wa Allahu Akbar.' This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence, allowing worshippers to maintain the essential essence of dhikr while accommodating varying levels of recitation capacity during prayer.
